impostor.title: Impostor syndrome
take.title: Take one of these back to your team
take.description: Nothing here is graded and nothing is checked. Four of the five are things to work out rather than things to build, so the tick is a bookmark.
take.queue.label: Write down what stands between your work being finished and it reaching production, and cross off anything that is typing.
take.sentence.label: Write the line you will say at the next demo about what the rough version does not do yet.
take.line.label: Pick one correction you gave an agent more than once this week and write it into the repository's own instruction file.
take.practice.label: Pick one ritual your team keeps, write down the constraint it was built for, and say whether that constraint is still there.
take.person.label: Put one of the first four in front of one person on your team. A name and a date.
pipeline-shift.description: The same five stages twice, drawn on one scale. Above, the way it ran when a person typed the code: deciding, waiting, a wide block of writing, verifying, releasing. Below, the way it runs with agents: writing is a sliver run as three lanes at once, verifying is the widest solid block, and both waiting stages are wider than they were. Under that second row, a dashed strip shows the verifying three lanes need. It runs well past the block above it, and a mark on it shows where the checking actually stopped.
pipeline-shift.caption: The times are illustrative. The scale is not: both rows are drawn against one clock, and the strip under the second is three lanes of output at what one lane cost to read.
quiz.three-weeks-after-thursday.question: You demo a working feature on Thursday and the room agrees it is done. Three weeks later you are still writing code on it, and nothing is waiting on a review or a release window. What ate the three weeks?
quiz.three-weeks-after-thursday.cases: The cases nobody had in mind when the request was written, some of which did not exist until the thing was half built.
quiz.three-weeks-after-thursday.vague: The request was too vague. A sharper one would have produced those cases in the first run.
quiz.three-weeks-after-thursday.poor: The agent's implementation was poor, so most of it had to be written again by hand.
quiz.three-weeks-after-thursday.queue: The queue: review, an environment nobody had provisioned, and the release window.
quiz.three-weeks-after-thursday.explanat: An agent implements the request it was given, along the path you described. A sharper first draft does not produce the detail nobody knew about yet, so the burden moved rather than lifted.
quiz.their-prototype.question: A manager built a working prototype over lunch and shows it in your meeting. It has no validation and one hard-coded member. What do you do?
quiz.their-prototype.say: Say what it does not do yet, out loud, in that meeting.
quiz.their-prototype.theirs: Say nothing. It is their prototype, so the caveats are theirs to give.
quiz.their-prototype.ticket: Write the gaps into a ticket, where the people who decide will read them.
quiz.their-prototype.build: Build the real version first, then show what a finished one looks like.
quiz.their-prototype.explanation: The sentence gets said either way. Left out now, it is said later by somebody asking why the feature they signed off on falls over on an empty list.
quiz.one-afternoon-quarter.question: Work that would have taken a week came back in an afternoon. Your manager asks what the team can commit to for the quarter. What do you give them?
quiz.one-afternoon-quarter.checkpoint: The next checkpoint and what will be true by then, because the afternoon is one sample.
quiz.one-afternoon-quarter.fourtimes: Four times the old output, since the afternoon is what the new rate looks like.
quiz.one-afternoon-quarter.old: The old estimate, since one fast run says nothing about a quarter.
quiz.one-afternoon-quarter.average: The average of the last three runs, which is as close to a rate as you can get.
quiz.one-afternoon-quarter.explanation: Hand the same request over twice and it does not come back the same twice. Your old estimate and your manager's read on quality are both readings of a job that changed shape, so the honest promise is the next checkpoint.
deck.change.test-engineer.title: You are <hi>the test engineer</hi> now
deck.change.test-engineer.note: Reading every line stops scaling. The case the agent did not think of does.
deck.change.business.title: Knowing the domain is <hi>not scope creep</hi>
deck.change.business.note: A version by Thursday only helps if somebody who knows what it was for looks at it on Thursday.
deck.change.pipelines.title: The process was <hi>the bottleneck</hi>
deck.change.rethink.title: The way of working is <hi>a decision</hi>
deck.change.rethink.2: Review, when <mute>an agent wrote the diff</mute>
deck.change.gates.title: Taste relaxes. <hi>The gates do not.</hi>
deck.change.environment.title: The deliverable is <hi>the environment</hi>, <mute>not this quarter</mute>
deck.change.environment.note: Count the times this week you told an agent something you had told it before. Each one is a line missing from a file.
deck.expectations.floor.title: A gain your competitor also gets is <hi>a floor</hi>, <mute>not a lead</mute>
deck.expectations.missing.title: Say what is missing <hi>when you show it</hi>
deck.expectations.missing.note: That sentence gets said either way. Later, and from a worse position.
deck.expectations.burden.title: The burden moved. <hi>It did not lift.</hi>
deck.expectations.burden.note: Finished Thursday, then three more weeks on the cases nobody could have written down.
deck.expectations.estimate.title: Say the date <hi>including the checking</hi>
deck.expectations.estimate.note: They got faster. Your reading did not. Otherwise "done" means two things in one room.
deck.expectations.velocity.title: One good run is not <hi>a velocity</hi>
deck.expectations.velocity.note: Promise the next checkpoint, not the finish.
deck.impostor.engineer.title: You are still <hi>the engineer</hi>
deck.impostor.engineer.note: The route was the agent's. The goal, the check and the reading were yours.
deck.impostor.signal.title: Tell the feeling from <hi>the signal</hi>
deck.impostor.signal.note: A diff you cannot follow is a gap with a fix.
deck.impostor.written.title: Nobody has been doing this <hi>long</hi>
deck.impostor.written.note: The tools changed twice while this course was written. A file that stopped needing the same correction is the only record of that.
deck.change.divider.1: Producing code is not the job
deck.change.divider.2: Business joins weekly, <mute>not at the demo</mute>
deck.change.divider.3: Typing was never what the calendar waited on
deck.expectations.divider.1: They saw an afternoon, <mute>and priced everything at one</mute>
deck.expectations.divider.2: The estimate still includes the checking
deck.impostor.divider.1: It lands when the agent is <hi>good</hi>
deck.impostor.divider.2: Judgement shows nothing at five o'clock
deck.impostor.divider.3: What adds up is <hi>what you wrote down</hi>
